report:
Liver allograft, post-reperfusion biopsy

Sections show a wedge biopsy of donor liver taken after reperfusion, with 11 portal tracts. Large-droplet steatosis involves about 5% of the parenchyma, and there is no small-droplet steatosis. There is moderate ischaemia-reperfusion injury, with clusters of sinusoidal neutrophils. Necrosis involves about 20% of the parenchyma, in zone 3. The portal tracts show minimal inflammation. There is no fibrosis. Cholestasis and lipofuscin pigment are seen. No granuloma or neoplasm is seen.

LIVER ALLOGRAFT, post-reperfusion biopsy - MODERATE ISCHAEMIA-REPERFUSION INJURY with ZONE 3 NECROSIS (20%), LARGE-DROPLET STEATOSIS (5%) and NO FIBROSIS

checks.message: Necrosis 20%: 10% or more may make a graft unsuitable, though up to 50% has been used, especially from brain-dead donors (Clin Transplant Res 2025).
